confirmedFindings.description: Open-return candidates enter owned state before validation; malformed or duplicated descriptor returns can reach cleanup and cause duplicate or unintended close.
When transaction body and release identity checks both fail, the outer error loses the sanitized original release cause.
The first lazy requests-stream binding uses a mutable diagnostics path rather than the frozen scope-derived path.

proposedGroupedCorrection: Validate candidate descriptor type and distinct ownership before committing cleanup state; deduplicate release and never retry uncertain descriptor closes.
Preserve sanitized release-phase original cause separately from body and cleanup failures.
Freeze the scope-derived requests path and revalidate diagnostics context before lazy registration.
Add direct regressions for malformed/duplicate open returns, combined body-and-release identity failure, and pre-registration path drift.
remainingGates: Bounded lifecycle cleanup and lock-release acceptance
Freshly authorized Linux native tests and database compatibility
Separately authorized production maintenance and actual-use acceptance
